title: Metro Brands Ltd - 543426 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Metro Brands Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 12.2% to INR730 crore, with EBITDA up 15.9% to INR198 crore, while festive demand shifted into Q3.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 12.2% to INR730 crore and EBITDA rose 15.9% to INR198 crore, with margin at 27.1% versus 26.2% a year ago. PAT grew about 11% to INR77 crore with margin flat at 10.6%, as higher rentals, staff costs and marketing, plus lower treasury income, offset a gross margin gain. Management attributed much of the revenue slowdown to festive demand moving from September into October, and said net store additions were slowed to 12 in Q2 with selective openings. Newer brands (Clarks, Foot Locker, MetroActiv, FILA) remain constrained by BIS-related supply issues and are being scaled cautiously.

financial_highlights.change: lower vs prior strong treasury year; FY26 full-year other income about INR100 crore

segments.name: Metro / Mochi / Walkway / own brands
segments.commentary: Own brands contributed about 70% of store product sales at Metro, Mochi and Walkway in H1. Walkway: over 35 stores opened in last 12-14 months on a base of about 60-70; roughly 30% performed well, 30% average, 30% poor.

segments.name: Crocs
segments.commentary: Crocs is under 20% of total business across stores, Metro and Mochi multi-brand. Management said Crocs grew decently and Durga Puja/Shraddh timing, not Crocs, drove the quarter.

segments.name: Clarks
segments.commentary: Women's range in more than 400 multi-brand outlets and limited men's range in more than 100; full exclusive store range expected in Q3 FY27, exclusive EBO launch targeted in H2 FY27. Clarks had about 80 EBOs in India at one point.

segments.name: FILA
segments.commentary: Local footwear manufacturing started in India in response to BIS concerns; repositioning expected over 12-18 months, with store expansion picking up from FY28.

segments.name: Foot Locker / MetroActiv
segments.commentary: BIS implementation challenges for selected external brands constrained supply and store expansion; early signs of normalisation, with openings calibrated to product availability.

guidance_outlook: PAT margin: management sees a medium- to long-term range of about 13%-15%, with 15% as the target once newer businesses scale; H2 PAT expected to be better than H1.
Store additions: H2 expected to exceed H1 in net openings; H1 had 34 openings and 13 closures, ending at 1,053 stores; store closures expected at about 2%-3% for the year.
Frontline staff costs expected to rise 0.5%-1% from the remuneration revision, offset if top-line improves.
Marketing spend expected at around 4% of revenue for the full year and next year.
Capex guidance: INR80-100 crore for FY27 including remodels, described as around INR100 crore.
Working capital: inventory to normalise by March 2027 partly, with 80-odd working capital days around mid-to-end FY28; ideal inventory about 7 months.
capex_capacity: Capex guidance for FY27 and FY28 is INR80-100 crore, including remodels; management cited around INR100 crore.
Store network 1,053 at end-September 2026; H1 openings 34, closures 13.
Clarks exclusive EBO launch expected in H2 FY27, subject to supply chain and assortment stabilisation.
FILA store expansion to pick up from FY28; medium-term aspiration of several hundred stores for FILA in 2-3 years.
Inventory-heavy: front-loaded stock for raw material inflation, FitFlop BIS renewals and Clarks/Foot Locker door fills.
demand_pricing: Festive demand shifted from September into October; Durga Puja moved out of Q2 and Shraddh fell fully inside Q2, estimated 250-350 bps impact on growth, per management.
Gross margin gain in Q2 driven by lower end-of-season discounts, slight markup improvement and lower e-commerce mix; management said the discount benefit will not sustain into Q3.
Raw material inflation about 10%-15%; price hikes on raw material pass-through about 2%-4%, possibly 2%-5%, varying by article.
Management said October festive trends look good, with Durga Puja performing well and other markets indicating a good festive season.
Management sees landlord pressure from rental inflation: limited supply of new retail space, one-and-done negotiations; cited rising rents and new players competing for space.

qa_highlights.question: Why were store closures and the H1 store addition pace so low versus the 100-110 average adds?
qa_highlights.answer: Closures are not format-specific and are reviewed on a two-year profitability test; FY closures expected at 2-3%. Management said rentals are high and supply is tight, and it is not fixated on a number, having opened over 100 doors last year.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the gross margin gain is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower end-of-season discounts and online sales discounts were the main drivers, with some markup improvement and lower e-commerce mix. Management said discount benefits will not sustain in Q3; mix shift towards Walkway, Foot Locker and MetroActiv may pull gross margin lower over time.

qa_highlights.question: Is the PAT margin pressure driven by rentals, staff costs and throughput?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO confirmed rental and minimum-wage-led staff cost pressure, talent and marketing investment, and lower treasury income (H1 other income about INR54 crore). Benefits from Clarks EBOs and marketing are expected from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the real underlying sales growth excluding festive and Crocs timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the shortfall to the Durga Puja and Shraddh shift, estimated at 250-350 bps, which takes growth back to about 15%. Crocs is under 20% of the business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory normalisation path?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory was front-loaded for raw material inflation, FitFlop BIS renewals and new door fills. Partial improvement by March 2027, return to about 80 working capital days around mid-to-end FY28, and ideal inventory about 7 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the marketing spend and capex outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Marketing spend about 4% of revenue in H1 versus 3.25%-3.4% a year ago, expected to stay around 4%. Capex guidance is INR80-100 crore for FY27 and FY28, including remodels.

risks_watch: Rental inflation and staff cost increases compressing PAT margin; H1 PAT margin about 160 bps below prior year on a pre-Ind AS basis, per analyst.
BIS licensing uncertainty for imported brands (Foot Locker, FILA, FitFlop, MetroActiv), delaying store expansion.
Inventory levels elevated; normalisation to about 80 working capital days targeted only in mid-to-end FY28.
Lower treasury income reducing other income versus a strong prior-year base.
Clarks EBO launch timing and execution, as management has no prior direct EBO experience with the brand.
Walkway new store productivity: about 30% of the 35-odd openings were weak, with the new-store format not yet cracked.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the brand portfolio and festive outlook, but candid and cautious on newer formats, with the PAT margin pressure and BIS-linked supply constraints acknowledged openly. Management was defensive when asked about store addition slowdown and rentals, emphasising disciplined, profitable openings over store count.
key_quotes: We recognize the difference between our revenue growth and bottom line growth.
So we don't really mind whether we open 70 stores or 125 stores if we believe they all have a chance of profitability.
15% PAT is like a medium- to long-term guidance we would want to be in that range of around 13% to 15%, especially considering investment that we are doing in the newer business.

adds.what: Store network additions: H1 FY27 34 openings, 13 closures, ending at 1,053 stores; H2 net additions expected to exceed H1
Clarks exclusive EBO launch (targeted H2 FY27, subject to supply chain stabilisation)
FILA store expansion picking up from FY28; aspiration of several hundred stores in 2-3 years

growth.why: Management guides H2 net store additions above H1 and FILA/Clarks expansion from H2 FY27/FY28, backed by stated capex of INR80-100 crore and a 13-15% medium-term PAT margin range, but no revenue growth figure is guided and Q2 festive timing and BIS supply constraints temper visibility.
